metadata.purpose: Enumerate, track, and resolve all ontological issues affecting cross-platform determinism (OI-001..OI-016)

issues.title: Windows CI runner line-ending mismatch
issues.description: Python scripts checked out on Windows received CRLF line endings, causing hash mismatches vs UTF-8 LF on Linux/macOS.
issues.resolution_notes: PR #27 added .gitattributes with text=auto eol=lf for all Python/YAML/JSON files; CI now normalises line endings at checkout.

issues.title: Missing PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 on Windows
issues.description: Windows CI runners default to cp1252 stdout encoding, breaking any code that writes UTF-8 characters to stdout/stderr.
issues.resolution_notes: PR #27 and PR #28 CI YAML set env PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8 at workflow level for all jobs.

issues.title: Integer arithmetic endianness sensitivity
issues.description: Weight generation code used platform-native integer arithmetic. On big-endian or 32-bit platforms the output differed.
issues.resolution_notes: Determinism test (test_cross_platform_determinism.py) uses bitwise two's-complement int64 arithmetic (platform-independent). Merkle root verified identical across Ubuntu, macOS, Windows.

issues.title: Filesystem path separator differences
issues.description: Hard-coded forward-slash paths failed on Windows where os.sep is backslash.
issues.resolution_notes: All path construction now uses pathlib.Path, which is cross-platform.

issues.title: safetensors int64 incompatibility
issues.description: safetensors >= 0.4 changed int64 handling, causing CI failures on older pinned versions.
issues.resolution_notes: PR #27 pinned safetensors to a compatible version and added pip install --upgrade to ensure correct resolution.

issues.title: Python version matrix not exhaustive
issues.description: CI only tested Python 3.11; 3.12 behavioural differences (e.g. hash randomisation seed) were untested.
issues.resolution_notes: PR #28 CI matrix includes python-version: ['3.11', '3.12'] across all three OS runners.

issues.title: Merkle root not compared cross-platform
issues.description: Previous CI computed a Merkle root on Linux only; no cross-OS comparison was performed.
issues.resolution_notes: PR #28 CI uploads the Merkle root from each OS as an artifact; the compare-merkle-roots job downloads all six (3 OS × 2 Python versions) and asserts equality, failing the build on any mismatch.

issues.title: No falsification test for seed_bytes assumption
issues.description: The spec assumed seed_bytes is interpreted identically on all platforms, but this was never tested.
issues.resolution_notes: test_falsification.py validates: seed_bytes round-trips through hashlib.sha256 identically, int64 two's-complement arithmetic matches expected vectors, UTF-8 encoding of output is preserved, pathlib paths resolve consistently.

issues.title: No strategic knowledge document for future contributors
issues.description: All environmental assumptions and tactical lessons were buried in PR history and chat logs, making them invisible to future AI/human contributors.
issues.resolution_notes: docs/ORTHOGONAL_ENGINEERING_COMPENDIUM.md created in PR #28. All environmental assumptions, tactical fixes, and verification procedures are documented there.

issues.title: Wall-clock timestamp leakage
issues.description: Code or CI steps that embed wall-clock timestamps or monotonic clocks make outputs non-reproducible. Two identical runs at different times produce different hashes.
issues.resolution_notes: blockchain_attestation.py requires timestamps to be externally supplied (not system clock). UVM uses a logical cycle_count, never wall-clock. CI workflows do not embed run timestamps in hashed artifacts.

issues.title: Hardware memory layout assumptions (NUMA / cache coherence)
issues.description: Code that relies on allocation order, cache-line alignment, or NUMA topology will produce different results on different hardware. Python's memory allocator is not guaranteed to be deterministic across OS / hardware.
issues.resolution_notes: UVM uses a dict-based memory model (no hardware RAM layout). All weight generation uses pure Python structures, not numpy/torch memory allocations, so NUMA topology is irrelevant.

issues.title: OS entropy source differences (/dev/urandom vs BCryptGenRandom)
issues.description: If weight generation or testing calls os.urandom() or secrets.token_bytes(), the outputs will differ across platforms because the OS PRNG seeds differ.
issues.resolution_notes: All randomness is derived deterministically from hashlib.sha256 of a fixed seed (CANONICAL_MERKLE_ROOT_SEED). No os.urandom() or secrets calls are made in weight generation or test code. F-001 falsification test verifies sha256 is byte-identical.

issues.title: Thread scheduling and GIL non-determinism
issues.description: Any multi-threaded or async code that writes shared state will produce different results depending on OS thread scheduler and GIL release points.
issues.resolution_notes: Current weight generation and test code is single-threaded. If parallel generation is introduced in future PRs, a deterministic task ordering layer must be added before that code may be merged.

issues.title: Python bytecode caching and JIT optimisation differences
issues.description: .pyc bytecode may differ between CPython versions and builds, affecting hash values if source files are hashed via their compiled form. PyPy JIT may produce different floating-point results.
issues.resolution_notes: All hashing operates on source bytes and data, never on .pyc files. No floating-point arithmetic is used in weight generation (all int64). PYTHONPYCACHEPREFIX is not set, so .pyc files do not affect determinism.

issues.title: Filesystem case sensitivity and symlink resolution differences
issues.description: macOS HFS+ is case-insensitive by default; Linux ext4 is case-sensitive. A file named 'Seed.yaml' may resolve to 'seed.yaml' on macOS but not on Linux. Symlinks may resolve differently.
issues.resolution_notes: All filenames in this repository use lowercase snake_case to avoid case ambiguity. Symlinks are not used. A linting rule should be added in a future PR to enforce lowercase filenames in tracked paths.

issues.title: Network non-determinism (DNS, NTP, certificate stores)
issues.description: Any CI step that makes network calls (DNS resolution, NTP sync, certificate validation, pip install from index) introduces external state that may differ across runners and time.
issues.resolution_notes: Weight generation and test code make no network calls. pip install is used in CI (network-dependent), but pip outputs are not hashed. Future work: pin pip dependencies to hashes in requirements.txt and use --no-index where possible.
